players.note: Fred Warner was excellent in Week 5, posting five solos, five assists, and one forced fumble. Warner has been locked in as a top-10 option and can be counted as a top-five play for Week 6, thanks to a plus matchup against Washington on Monday Night Football.

Ernest Jones was at it again in Week 5, posting five solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Jones has ridden one splash week and two spike weeks to LB2 status through five weeks of action and deserves to be treated as an elite top-five option while he is cooking.

Nakobe Dean stayed hot in Week 5, racking up five solos and five assists. Dean has registered two splash weeks and two spike weeks and checks into Week 6 as the LB1 overall. Tap Dean as a top-five option as long as he is on fire. Start Nakobe everywhere.

Alex Singleton stayed hot in Week 5, notching five solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Singleton has four spike weeks to his name, cementing him as an LB1 play going forward. The LB14 through five weeks of action, tap Singleton as a top-12 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.
Roquan Smith showed up in Week 5, racking up five solos and three assists. Roquan has one splash week and one spike week to his name and should continue to be treated as a top-12 option.

Carson Schwesinger was at it again in Week 5, notching five solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Carson has been locked in as a top-10 option, popping with a splash or spike week in three of his five games. He is dealing with an ankle injury, but if he is active, start the Browns linebacker everywhere as an LB1 play.

Zack Baun was at it again in Week 5, racking up six solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. Baun has registered three spike weeks in four contests, cementing him as a top-10 option for Week 6 and beyond. Start him everywhere for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Foyesade Oluokun showed up in Week 5, tallying six solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Foye was a LB2 option after three weeks but back in the LB1 conversation thanks to two spike weeks and one splash week. Oluokun is safe to count as a top-12 option again. Treat him as such for a tasty Week 6 matchup against the Houston Texans on Sunday morning.

Arvell Reese was at it again in Week 5, racking up three solos, six assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Reese has now registered two splash weeks followed by a spike week, vaulting him to LB3 overall on the season. Tap Arvell as a top-10 option as long as he is cooking.

Tremaine Edmunds stayed hot in Week 5, tallying six solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Edmunds has one splash week and three spike weeks to his name, placing him as the LB10 through five weeks of play. Treat Edmunds as a top-12 play as long as he is in vintage form.

Nate Landman showed out on Monday Night Football, racking up eight solos, five assists, one tackle for loss, and two forced fumbles. Landman was in the midst of a slow start to the season before the breakout game, but has still recorded four or more solos in three of five. He is the LB24 on the season but can still be counted as a top-15 option for Week 6, thanks to a plus matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Josiah Trotter was excellent in Week 5, racking up five solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Trotter has three spike weeks to go with the massive splash week in his NFL debut, solidifying him as a top-five option as long as he is on fire. Start Trotter as an elite LB1 play for Week 6 against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Azeez Al-Shaair was at it again in Week 5, tallying five solos, six assists, and one pass defended. Al-Shaair has recorded three spike weeks in four games, settling him in as a safe top-20 option. Tap Azeez as an elite LB2 play for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Payton Wilson stayed hot in Week 5, tallying eight solos, two assists, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Wilson has recorded two straight splash weeks to go with his two spike weeks, placing him as the LB8 through five weeks of action. Count Wilson as a top-12 option while he's cooking

Devin Lloyd returned to action in Week 4, racking up five solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Despite missing a game, Lloyd has been the top fantasy linebacker in both total points and fantasy points per game through four weeks of action. Lloyd has solidified himself as a top-five option until further notice. Start him everywhere as an IDP1 candidate.

Zaire Franklin was excellent in Week 5, reeling off five solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Zaire should soak up more tackles with Edgerrin Cooper lost for the season and can be counted as a strong LB2 option. Tap Franklin as a top-25 play for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Sonny Styles was excellent in Week 5, tallying four solos, nine assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Styles has registered three spike weeks despite failing to top four solos all season. The rookie linebacker should only get better as the season progresses and is already locked in as a top-20 option. Treat him as just that for Monday Night Football against the San Francisco 49ers.

Devin Bush showed up in Week 5, recording three solos, five assists, and two tackles for loss. It was the first spike week of the season for Bush, who has yet to top three solos all season. Treat the Bears linebacker as a low floor LB3 option for Week 6.

Quincy Williams was excellent in Week 5, reeling off seven solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, three forced fumbles, and one pass defended. Williams is a strong LB2 option and should be targeted as such for a tasty Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Frankie Luvu showed up in Week 5, tallying six solos and three assists. Luvu was injured in Week 1, causing him to miss two weeks of action. Luvu has proven LB2 upside, but based on last season and a potentially injury-fueled slow start to the season, it is better to view him as an LB3 play until he proves otherwise. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football.

Drue Tranquill showed up in Week 4, reeling off five solos, two assists, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. The LB24 through four weeks of action, thanks to two spike weeks, Drue can be counted as a top-25 option as long as he is cooking. Treat him as such for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Jake Hansen showed up in Week 5, reeling off three solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Hansen had a splash week in Week 4, and now with a spike week in Week 5, Hansen has forced his way into must-start LB3 territory. His upside has been plain for all to see, making Hansen an ideal plug-and-play option until Henry To'oTo'o returns.

Jaden Dugger stepped up in Week 5, racking up seven solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Dugger saw an expanded role with Dre Greenlaw ejected and should see one again this week with Dre suspended for one game. It was an impressive performance for the firth round rookie, who will be able to solidify an expanded role even when Greenlaw returns with another strong outing. Treat Dugger as an LB4/flex with LB3 upside for Week 6.

Isaiah McDuffie was tapped by many fantasy managers as the linebacker expected to draw the starts with star linebacker Edgerrin Cooper lost for the season. Instead, it was Ty'ron Hopper who played 57 percent of the snaps while McDuffie handled just 46 percent. McDuffie has enough upside to be worth holding onto for at least one more week, but should not sniff fantasy lineups given the rotation we saw in Week 5. Look elsewhere for Week 6.

Pete Werner stepped up in Week 5, notching four solos and six assists on 100 percent of the snaps. Werner has seen an expanded role over the last two weeks due to Kaden Elliss dealing with a calf injury. Werner was trending as an LB3 prior to Elliss being sidelined, but should now be considered part of the top-25 conversation for as long as Kaden is sidelined. Werner has one splash week and two near spike weeks to his name and has managed to stay fantasy relevant despite splitting time with Danny Stutsman. Start Werner as an LB2 while Elliss is out and an LB3 when he returns.

Dee Winters showed up in Week 5, racking up six solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Winters has proven to be a solid LB3 play so far, with two games with six or more solos and four games with four or more. There was an expectation that Winters would see an everydown role for Dallas, but his issues in coverage and lack of playcalling/green dot acumen have kept him closer to the 70 percent range most weeks, effectively capping his upside and dropping his floor; hence the LB3 tag. Tap Winters as a top-36 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Trenton Simpson stayed hot in Week 5, racking up five solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss under the bright lights of Sunday Night Football. Simpson has now recorded a spike week in three straight games and is still hovering around the 55-60 snap share mark despite Teddye Buchanan seeing his own snaps expanded. This suggests that Simpson is locked into his role until further notice, which should be all the impetus fantasy managers need to make him a priority add this week. The LB12 through five weeks of action, the Ravens linebacker should be rostered in all competitive leagues; act accordingly.

Cody Barton has played 83 percent and 97 percent of the snaps in Week 4 and Week 5, respectively, but even with three games north of 80 percent of the snaps (97 percent in Week 1), Barton has failed to make much of a fantasy impact. Barton has remained a starter despite the return of Cedric Gray, as the coaching staff prefers having him next to rookie Anthony Hill to help him with processing his MIKE duties. Barton has topped three solos just once all season (four solos in Week 4) and needs to show more to be trusted as a flex option over defensive backs with more upside. Feel free to ignore Barton outs
ide of 16+ team leagues.

Justin Strnad showed up in Week 5, racking up five solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. It was the first spike week of the season for Strnad, who saw a season high in snaps with both Pat Surtain and Riley Moss ruled out. Strnad becomes an option when four teams are on bye, so tap him as an LB4/flex2 option where needed for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

Danielle Hunter showed up in Week 5, notching three solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Hunter has just two spike weeks ot his name but has recorded at least a half sack in four straight games. He is up to a solid enough three sacks on the season and remains a top-12 option due to his propensity to get sacks in bunches. Treat him as such for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Kendall Daniels stepped up in Week 5, tallying seven solos, one assist, and one sack. Daniels saw 65 percent of the snaps in Week 5, with the Falcons placing a premium on stopping Derrick Henry on the ground. Daniels sees backup snaps against passing offenses due to his issues in coverage, but should see starter snaps again in Week 6, thanks to a date with the Chicago Bears. Daniels is an LB4 type who can be an LB3 during the byes.

Nik Bonitto was at it again in Week 5, tallying three solos, one assist, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Bonitto is up to three sacks on the season, with all three coming in his last three games. Bonitto is one of the best in the league when he is on, and his recent production suggests that he is ready to roll. Tap him as a top-10 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Abdul Carter stepped up in Week 5, tallying two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. It was just the second sack of the season for Carter, who is facing more double teams with Brian Burns lost for the season. This was supposed to be a breakout season for the Giants pass rusher, and while he remains a pressure machine, they have not been translating to sacks. Count Carter as more DL2 than DL1 until he starts to heat up for the Giants, but don't put him on your bench. Carter is an elite talent who should start to get sacks in bunches. Tap Carter as a top-25 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. Start Carter everywhere.

Josh Hines-Allen showed up in Week 4, tallying four solos and two tackles for loss. Hines-Allen has not recorded a sack since Week 1 and still sits at 1.5 sacks for the season. Treat the Jaguars edge rusher as a DL2/Dl3 type until he starts to get rolling.

David Bailey showed out in Week 5, racking up five solos, two assists, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. Bailey is now up to five sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of the first five games of his career. The DL3 in total fantasy points after the splash week, Bailey can now be counted as a top-15 option going forward.

Elijah Ponder was at it again in Week 5, racking up four solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Ponder is up to a new career high of 4.5 sacks and should have at least a few more weeks of starter-level snaps while Harold Landry remains on the mend. Ponder has a tasty matchup in Week 5 against the New York Jets, making him a DL2 option. Tap Ponder as a top-25 option as long as he is cooking.

Austin Booker was excellent in Week 5, racking up four solos, one assist, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Booker is up to four sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his last four games. Tap Booker as a top-25 option for Week 6, thanks both to his hot streak and a plus matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Carl Granderson showed up in Week 5, racking up two solos, three assists, 1.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. Granderson is up to 2.5 sacks on the season and is a solid DL3 during the byes, including this week, thanks to a plus Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants.

Mike Green was excellent in Week 5, racking up two solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Green is up to two sacks on the season and makes for a solid DL3 option for Week 6, thanks to a tasty matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Start the Ravens pass rusher where needed.

Tavius Robinson showed out in Week 5, racking up three solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Tavius is up to three sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his five games. The DL22 through five weeks of action, Robinson should be counted as an elite DL3 option for Week 6, thanks to a tasty matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Akheem Mesidor stepped up in Week 5, tallying five solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Mesidor is up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with a sack in two of his last three games. Akheem has looked the part through the first five weeks of the season and may be set to see an expanded role in the near future with Khalil Mack emerging as one of the hottest trade candidates in the league. Mesidor should be rostered in all leagues as a bye week depth piece who could emerge as a DL2/3 option in the next couple of weeks.

Princely Umanmielen was at it again in Week 4, racking up three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss on a season high 52 percent of the snaps. Princely has been a force off the edge for the Panthers, recording a sack in three of his first four contests of the season. He could see an expanded role in Week 6 if Jaelan Phillips sees his snaps scaled back in an effort to prevent further injury. If Jaelan Phillips misses Week 6, Umanmielen becomes a must-start DL3 with DL2 upside.

K'Lavon Chaisson showed up in Week 5, reeling off one solo, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Chaisson has zero spike weeks but is up to a solid 2.5 sacks on the season, with at least a half sack in three of his last four games. K'Lavon can be counted as a top-36 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Keion White was excellent in Week 5, racking up three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Keion is now up to three sacks on the season and has recorded at least one sack in three of his last four games. White has seen an expanded role over the last two weeks due to Nick Bosa being sidelined with a quad injury and has produced well enough to factor prominently in the rotation until he cools down.

Dani Dennis-Sutton stepped up in Week 5, tallying three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. DDS is up to 1.5 sacks on the season and is playing enough to be a deep league option during the byes. With Micah Parsons not yet ready to return for Week 6, Sutton becomes a DL3/4 option for a plus matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Baron Browning showed up in Week 5, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and two forced fumbles on 43 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Browning, who is more of a deep league bench option than someone those in 12 team leagues should have on their radars, at least for now.
